; Set A=Y=0, write mapper selector zero and continue at bank zero's reset entry $8001. Identical
; CPU addresses in other banks remain separate physical entries.
; Ascending mapper-write values $00..$13. Reset uses the first value; other consumers remain
; unresolved. These bytes are data, not entry points.
; Single zero byte at the repeated bank boundary, before the reset entry or between mapper values
; and hardware vectors. The repeated layout fixes this extent; no unused/dead claim is made.
; Little-endian NMI/reset/IRQ vectors ($8095/$ffdc/$8367). A vector value alone does not establish
; interrupt reachability in every bank.
; Shared CPU RAM and NES hardware symbols. Exact values preserve instruction widths.
; Zero-page arrays use player slot X/Y in court code; menus reuse the same bytes.
; SourcePointer and scratch bytes are call-clobbered; meaning is local to a routine.
; PlayerDirection: 0 right, 1 left, 2 down, 3 up, 4..7 diagonals.
; PlayerInput bits: $01 right, $02 left, $04 down, $08 up, $10 Start,
; $20 Select, $40 B, $80 A. Computer control generates the same bit format.
; BallOwner/BallActionPlayer use negative values for no owner.
; Clock/score fields hold ASCII digits. QuarterIndex is zero-based.
; Graphics use CHR RAM; PPU addresses are separate from CPU/physical ROM addresses.
; Target horizontal span seeds the signed axis-error pair; depth span is its unsigned magnitude.
; Subtract depth span until negative, then add the retained horizontal span to step depth.
